newsitem.title: UK: Future US air cargo trade index up 2.3pct in Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: Future US air cargo trade index up 2.3pct in Oct 9.

text.p: The index of future U.S. air cargo business rose 1.4 percent to 528.7 in October, compared to a 3.3 percent gain in September, the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi said.
In its latest foreign trade survey of air freight carriers, seaports and trucking firms, the bank's New York economic research department said the import growth was relatively steady in October.
The three month forward looking index said air cargo expectations were up 1.2 percent to 674.50, against a 3.2 percent rise in September.
There was a increase in air cargo import expectations which gained 1.7 percent from 3.5 percent the previous month.
In October the air cargo export conditions rose by 0.5 percent in October, while import conditions jumped by 4.5 percent, the survey said.
The index is an equally weighted composite index of current export and import air cargo activity (not seasonally adjusted and 1989 equals 100).
Survey participants said the key trade concern for 1997 is likely to be the foreign exchange value of the dollar, "yet few ventured a forecast of the direction and magnitude of the dollar's change."

Other important trade issues for the new year were cited by industry executives included the U.S. Administration's position on trade with China, and the on-going embargo with Cuba. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
